Turkish · 1,000 words

The 100 most common Turkish words

The 100 Turkish words you'll hear most often, each with its meaning in English, an example sentence and, for verbs, the main forms (he, she or it). 99 of them are taught in the lessons of the course.

Learn them with spaced repetition, Anki-style: open the flashcards. Free, no account needed.

Overview1–100101–200201–300301–400401–500501–600601–700701–800801–900901–1000
  1. 1
    birnumber

    one; a, an

    Bir çay, lütfen.

    One tea, please.

    As a, an it comes right before the noun, after any adjective: güzel bir ev (a nice house).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  2. 2
    olmakverb

    to be; to become; to happen

    Ne oldu? Neden ağlıyorsun?

    What happened? Why are you crying?

    aorist olur · present oluyor · past oldu · future olacak

    One of the few one-syllable verbs with the aorist in -Ir: olur. On its own, Olur also means OK, sure.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company· Conjugation

  3. 3
    miparticle

    question particle (yes-no questions)

    Yorgun musun?

    Are you tired?

    Written as a separate word. Its vowel follows harmony (mı, mi, mu, mü) and it carries the personal ending: Hazır mısın?

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  4. 4
    bupronoun

    this; this one

    Bu ne?

    What is this?

    Case endings come after an n: bunu, buna, bunda. Plural bunlar (these).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  5. 5
    benpronoun

    I; me

    Ben öğretmenim, o öğrenci.

    I'm a teacher, she's a student.

    Usually dropped, since the verb ending already says I. Irregular dative bana (to me); also beni (me), benim (my).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  6. 6
    senpronoun

    you (one person, familiar)

    Ben iyiyim, sen nasılsın?

    I'm fine, how are you?

    Irregular dative sana (to you); also seni, senin (your). Use siz with strangers and older people.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  7. 7
    opronoun

    he, she, it; that (farther away)

    O benim en iyi arkadaşım.

    She's my best friend.

    One word for he, she and it. Case endings come after an n: onu, ona, onun.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  8. 8
    nepronoun

    what; how (in exclamations)

    Bu akşam ne yapıyorsun?

    What are you doing tonight?

    In exclamations it means how: Ne güzel! (How nice!). Ne … ne = neither … nor.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  9. 9
    deconjunction

    too, also; and; even

    Ayşe de bizimle geliyor.

    Ayşe is coming with us too.

    A separate word after the word it refers to: de after front vowels, da after back vowels (Ali de, Murat da). The locative suffix -de is attached.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  10. 10
    veconjunction

    and

    Ekmek ve peynir aldım.

    I bought bread and cheese.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  11. 11
    etmekverb

    to do, to make (with a noun)

    Bana yardım eder misin?

    Could you help me?

    aorist eder · present ediyor · past etti · future edecek

    Mostly a helper that turns a noun into a verb: yardım etmek (to help), dans etmek (to dance). t becomes d before a vowel: ediyor.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  12. 12
    yapmakverb

    to do; to make

    Hafta sonu ne yaptın?

    What did you do on the weekend?

    aorist yapar · present yapıyor · past yaptı · future yapacak

    Yemek yapmak = to cook.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  13. 13
    şeynoun

    thing; um, er (hesitation)

    Sana bir şey söyleyeceğim.

    I'm going to tell you something.

    Bir şey (something) and her şey (everything) are written as two words.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects

  14. 14
    içinpostposition

    for; in order to; because of

    Bu hediye senin için.

    This present is for you.

    Personal pronouns take the genitive: benim için (for me). After a verb in -mAk it means in order to: öğrenmek için.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  15. 15
    istemekverb

    to want; to ask for

    Ne istersin, çay mı kahve mi?

    What would you like, tea or coffee?

    aorist ister · present istiyor · past istedi · future isteyecek

    The e becomes i before -(I)yor: istiyorum.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  16. 16
    varadjective

    there is, there are; existing, present

    Evde süt var mı?

    Is there any milk at home?

    Says that something exists or is somewhere; the opposite is yok. Bir kardeşim var = I have a sibling.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  17. 17
    değilparticle

    not (with nouns and adjectives)

    Ben yorgun değilim.

    I'm not tired.

    Negates sentences without a verb and takes the personal ending: değilim, değilsin. Verbs use the suffix -mA instead.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  18. 18
    çokadverb

    very; a lot, much; many, a lot of

    Bu film çok güzel.

    This movie is very good.

    Before a noun it means many, a lot of, and the noun stays singular: çok insan (a lot of people).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  19. 19
    gelmekverb

    to come

    Yarın bize gelir misin?

    Will you come over tomorrow?

    aorist gelir · present geliyor · past geldi · future gelecek

    One of the few one-syllable verbs with the aorist in -Ir: gelir.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  20. 20
    bilmekverb

    to know; to know how to

    Bilmiyorum, ona sor.

    I don't know, ask him.

    aorist bilir · present biliyor · past bildi · future bilecek

    Aorist in -Ir: bilir. For knowing people, use tanımak.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  21. 21
    amaconjunction

    but

    Pahalı ama çok güzel.

    It's expensive, but really nice.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  22. 22
    gitmekverb

    to go

    Yarın İzmir'e gidiyorum.

    I'm going to Izmir tomorrow.

    aorist gider · present gidiyor · past gitti · future gidecek

    t becomes d before a vowel: gidiyor, gider, gidecek.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  23. 23
    evetinterjection

    yes

    Evet, haklısın.

    Yes, you're right.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  24. 24
    iyiadjective

    good; well, fine

    İyiyim, teşekkür ederim.

    I'm fine, thank you.

    İyi akşamlar (good evening), iyi geceler (good night), iyi günler (have a nice day).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  25. 25
    söylemekverb

    to say; to tell

    Ona doğruyu söyledim.

    I told him the truth.

    aorist söyler · present söylüyor · past söyledi · future söyleyecek

    The e becomes ü before -(I)yor: söylüyor. The person told takes the dative: ona söyle.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company· Conjugation

  26. 26
    buradaadverb

    here

    Anahtarlar burada.

    The keys are here.

    bura (this place) with the locative. Also buraya (to here), buradan (from here), burası (this place).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  27. 27
    almakverb

    to take; to buy; to get

    Fırından ekmek aldım.

    I bought bread at the bakery.

    aorist alır · present alıyor · past aldı · future alacak

    Aorist in -Ir: alır. Satın almak = to buy (more formal).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects· Conjugation

  28. 28
    hayırinterjection

    no

    Hayır, teşekkürler.

    No, thanks.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  29. 29
    vermekverb

    to give

    Bana tuzu verir misin?

    Could you pass me the salt?

    aorist verir · present veriyor · past verdi · future verecek

    Aorist in -Ir: verir. The receiver takes the dative: bana ver.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company· Conjugation

  30. 30
    demekverb

    to say; to mean; to call (a name)

    Bu kelime ne demek?

    What does this word mean?

    aorist der · present diyor · past dedi · future diyecek

    Irregular: diyor, diyecek. Demek ki means so, that means.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 4: Habits and truths: the aorist· Conjugation

  31. 31
    dahaadverb

    more; still, yet; -er (comparative)

    Biraz daha çay ister misin?

    Would you like a bit more tea?

    Makes comparatives: daha büyük (bigger). With a negative it means yet: Daha gelmedi (He hasn't come yet).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 1: The past tense

  32. 32
    bakmakverb

    to look (at); to look after

    Şu fotoğrafa bak!

    Look at this photo!

    aorist bakar · present bakıyor · past baktı · future bakacak

    Takes the dative: bana bak (look at me), çocuğa bakmak (to look after a child).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from· Conjugation

  33. 33
    yokadjective

    there is not, there are not; absent, missing

    Bugün okulda kimse yok.

    There's nobody at school today.

    The opposite of var. Param yok = I have no money.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  34. 34
    görmekverb

    to see

    Dün Ayşe'yi gördüm.

    I saw Ayşe yesterday.

    aorist görür · present görüyor · past gördü · future görecek

    Aorist in -Ir: görür.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects· Conjugation

  35. 35
    zamannoun

    time; when (ne zaman)

    Ne zaman geliyorsun?

    When are you coming?

    Ne zaman? = When? Hiç zamanım yok = I have no time at all.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  36. 36
    kadarpostposition

    until; as … as; about (with amounts)

    Saat beşe kadar çalışıyorum.

    I work until five o'clock.

    After the dative it means until: akşama kadar. After a noun, as … as: senin kadar uzun (as tall as you).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  37. 37
    gibipostposition

    like; as

    Kardeşim de senin gibi doktor.

    My sister is a doctor, like you.

    Personal pronouns take the genitive: benim gibi (like me).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 8: Comparing

  38. 38
    bizpronoun

    we; us

    Biz Ankara'da yaşıyoruz.

    We live in Ankara.

    Dative bize, accusative bizi, genitive bizim (our).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  39. 39
    tamaminterjection

    OK, all right; complete, finished

    Tamam, yarın görüşürüz.

    OK, see you tomorrow.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  40. 40
    işnoun

    work, job; business; matter, thing to do

    Yeni bir iş buldum.

    I found a new job.

    İşe gitmek = to go to work.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  41. 41
    sizpronoun

    you (plural); you (polite)

    Siz nerelisiniz?

    Where are you from?

    The plural you, and the polite you for one person. Dative size, genitive sizin (your).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  42. 42
    herdeterminer

    every; each

    Her sabah kahve içerim.

    I drink coffee every morning.

    Her şey (everything), her zaman (always), herkes (everyone).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 4: Habits and truths: the aorist

  43. 43
    biripronoun

    someone, somebody; one (of them)

    Kapıda biri var.

    There's someone at the door.

    Also birisi. İçlerinden biri = one of them.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 5: Can and can't

  44. 44
    nedenadverb

    why; reason

    Neden geç kaldın?

    Why are you late?

    Niye is a more casual why. As a noun, reason: Bunun nedeni ne?

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  45. 45
    kiconjunction

    that; so … that; who, which

    Öyle yorgunum ki uyuyamıyorum.

    I'm so tired that I can't sleep.

    Written apart as a conjunction. The suffix -ki is attached (evdeki), and it is fused in belki, çünkü, sanki.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 8: Small words: dA, bile, ki, ya

  46. 46
    nasıladverb

    how; what kind of

    Okula nasıl gidiyorsun?

    How do you get to school?

    Nasılsın? = How are you?

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  47. 47
    kendipronoun

    self (myself, yourself and so on); own

    Bunu kendim yaptım.

    I made this myself.

    Takes possessive endings: kendim, kendin, kendisi. Before a noun it means own: kendi evim (my own house).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 10: Passive and reflexive

  48. 48
    yaconjunction

    what about … (ya sen: what about you); either … or (ya … ya); or (ya da)

    Ben iyiyim, ya sen?

    I'm fine, and you?

    Ya da means or: çay ya da kahve. Alone it can also mean really? or oh.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  49. 49
    şupronoun

    that (nearby); this, the following

    Şu adamı tanıyor musun?

    Do you know that man?

    Points to something near the listener or about to be named. Case endings come after an n: şunu, şuna.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  50. 50
    kalmakverb

    to stay; to remain, to be left

    Bu akşam evde kalıyorum.

    I'm staying home tonight.

    aorist kalır · present kalıyor · past kaldı · future kalacak

    Aorist in -Ir: kalır. Geç kalmak = to be late.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 10: Whose is it?· Conjugation

  51. 51
    sadeceadverb

    only, just

    Sadece bir dakika bekle.

    Just wait a minute.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 1: Past continuous and pluperfect

  52. 52
    öyleadverb

    like that, so; such

    Öyle mi? Bilmiyordum.

    Really? I didn't know.

    Böyle (like this), şöyle (like this, as follows) and öyle (like that) go with bu, şu, o. Öyle mi? = Really?

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  53. 53
    adamnoun

    man; person, guy

    O adamı tanıyorum.

    I know that man.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 2: Was, were, and once upon a time

  54. 54
    düşünmekverb

    to think; to think about

    Seni düşünüyorum.

    I'm thinking of you.

    aorist düşünür · present düşünüyor · past düşündü · future düşünecek

    What you think about takes the accusative: seni düşünüyorum.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 4: Verbal nouns· Conjugation

  55. 55
    sonraadverb

    later, then; after

    Sonra konuşuruz.

    We'll talk later.

    After the ablative it means after: dersten sonra (after class).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  56. 56
    bulmakverb

    to find

    Anahtarımı bulamıyorum.

    I can't find my key.

    aorist bulur · present buluyor · past buldu · future bulacak

    Aorist in -Ir: bulur.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 10: Whose is it?· Conjugation

  57. 57
    hadiinterjection

    come on; let's

    Hadi, geç kalıyoruz!

    Come on, we're running late!

    Also haydi. Hadi gidelim = Let's go.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 7: Let's: suggestions and wishes

  58. 58
    yernoun

    place; ground, floor; seat, room

    Burada boş yer var mı?

    Is there a free seat here?

    Yere düştü = it fell on the floor. Yerine = instead of.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 5: Can and can't

  59. 59
    çıkmakverb

    to go out, to leave; to go up, to climb; to come out

    Saat sekizde evden çıktım.

    I left the house at eight.

    aorist çıkar · present çıkıyor · past çıktı · future çıkacak

    The place you leave takes the ablative: evden çıkmak; where you climb takes the dative: dağa çıkmak.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from· Conjugation

  60. 60
    şimdiadverb

    now

    Şimdi çok meşgulüm.

    I'm very busy right now.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous

  61. 61
    çalışmakverb

    to work; to study; to try

    Annem bir hastanede çalışıyor.

    My mother works at a hospital.

    aorist çalışır · present çalışıyor · past çalıştı · future çalışacak

    Sınava çalışmak = to study for an exam; -mAyA çalışmak = to try to.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  62. 62
    gerekmekverb

    to be necessary; to have to, to need (gerekiyor)

    Gitmem gerekiyor.

    I have to go.

    aorist gerekir · present gerekiyor · past gerekti · future gerekecek

    Used in the third person: gitmem gerekiyor is literally my going is necessary.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 5: Formal Turkish· Conjugation

  63. 63
    hiçadverb

    never, (not) at all; ever (in questions)

    Hiç İstanbul'a gittin mi?

    Have you ever been to Istanbul?

    With a negative verb: Hiç bilmiyorum (I have no idea at all).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous

  64. 64
    neredeadverb

    where

    Tuvalet nerede?

    Where's the washroom?

    Nereye (where to), nereden (where from), nereli (from where, of a person).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  65. 65
    onlarpronoun

    they; them

    Onlar yarın geliyorlar.

    They're coming tomorrow.

    Accusative onları, dative onlara, genitive onların (their). With onlar the plural ending of the verb is often left out.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  66. 66
    konuşmakverb

    to speak; to talk

    Türkçe konuşuyor musun?

    Do you speak Turkish?

    aorist konuşur · present konuşuyor · past konuştu · future konuşacak

    Biriyle konuşmak = to talk with someone.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  67. 67
    sanmakverb

    to think, to suppose; to believe (wrongly)

    aorist sanır · present sanıyor · past sandı · future sanacak

    Aorist in -Ir: sanır. Sanırım (I think) is very common.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 4: Habits and truths: the aorist· Conjugation

  68. 68
    enadverb

    most, -est (superlative)

    En iyi arkadaşım Can.

    My best friend is Can.

    Before an adjective: en iyi (best), en büyük (biggest).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 8: Comparing

  69. 69
    önceadverb

    before; ago; first

    kimpronoun

    who

    Bu çocuk kim?

    çocuknoun

    evnoun

    house, home

  73. 73
    ikinumber

    two

    İki çay, lütfen.

  74. 74
    günnoun

    day

    Bugün güzel bir gün.

  75. 75
    babanoun

    father, dad

    güzeladjective

    oradaadverb

    anlamakverb

    birazadverb

    kıznoun

    bırakmakverb

    to leave (somewhere); to let go; to quit

    aorist bırakır · present bırakıyor · past bıraktı · future bırakacak

    Aorist in -Ir: bırakır. Sigarayı bırakmak = to quit smoking.

  82. 82
    annenoun

    mother, mom

    Annem çok güzel yemek yapar.

    insannoun

    teşekkür ederimphrase

    thank you

    başkaadjective

    other, another; else

  86. 86
    sevmekverb

    to love; to like

    Kahveyi çok severim.

    I really like coffee.

About this list

The words are ranked by how often they come up in film and TV dialogue, so the list leans towards spoken Turkish. Words are listed in their dictionary form (verbs in the infinitive, gelmek), names and fragments are left out, and ranks are estimates rather than exact counts.

The order of the list is adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, made from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus via OPUS, and is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The meanings, example sentences and notes are original to Daily Turkish.
